errors.english: ### Chapter Twenty-One: Examination of Arising and Dissolution
errors.why: This is the closing colophon of chapter 21; the verses that follow begin chapter 22 (Examination of the Tathāgata), but the English turns the colophon into a heading over them.

fix.find: ### Chapter Twenty-One: Examination of Arising and Dissolution
fix.replace: This concludes the twenty-first chapter, the Examination of Arising and Dissolution.

errors.english:
Why would that which is unappropriated 
not become the appropriator?
errors.why: MMK 22.7: what is not appropriated in no way becomes an appropriation (ཅིས་མི་འགྱུར = 'in no way is'); the rhetorical question implies the opposite.

fix.find:
Why would that which is unappropriated 
not become the appropriator?
fix.replace:
That which has not been appropriated 
in no way becomes an appropriation.

note: End of MMK 21 and opening of MMK 22, mostly faithful, but the chapter colophon is misplaced as a heading and verse 22.7 is reversed.

errors.english: like the wish-fulfilling tree among the trees of the gods
errors.why: ཡོངས་འདུ is the pārijāta (the coral tree of the gods), not the wish-fulfilling tree (dpag bsam shing).

note: Faithful rendering of the ornate verses with the Sanskrit given in notes; only the pārijāta is mislabelled.

errors.why: ཕྱག་བྱ་བར་གྱུར་པ means having become one to whom homage is paid (the arhat is greeted first), not the arhat offering prostrations.

note: Accurate gloss-by-gloss commentary on arhat epithets; one gloss's direction is likely inverted.
Faithful rendering of Avalokitavrata's discussion of the 'vulnerable assertion' and the sound/pot example.
Accurate Vinaya commentary on consent and on a monk seized on the poṣadha day.
Faithful rendering of the Sautrāntika position and its refutation, root verse correctly set off.
Accurate rendering of the bowl and Dharma-teaching training rules with their origin stories.

errors.english: then this is merely the realm of aspiration
errors.why: The author concedes this horn ('this we simply accept') before attacking the Path-of-Seeing reading; the English turns the concession into a dismissal.
The Sanskrit for སེམས་བསྐྱེད་པ is cittotpāda, not 'cittapada'.

errors.english: because it depends on the desire for a perfect body and so forth
errors.why: The desired perfect body etc. depend on the abandonment of immorality (hence it is like the vase of plenty), not the reverse.

note: Sound translation of the bodhicitta-simile commentary, with a mis-spelled Sanskrit gloss and two clauses whose logic is turned around.

errors.english: it should be viewed as a consciousness that is a subversion of the essential nature as previously explained
errors.why: Ignorance is to be seen as having the nature already explained, namely an inverted (viparyasta) cognition; it is not a 'subversion of the essential nature'.

note: Generally accurate rendering of the Daśabhūmika quotation and the argument on ignorance and satkāyadṛṣṭi, with messy inline glosses.
Faithful rendering of the argument that sense-function is known by inference and yogic perception makes the past manifest.
